question:
A 25-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of nosebleeds over the past 6 months. The nosebleeds occur spontaneously and stop after 10 minutes after pinching the nose at the nostrils. He has no history of serious illness except for prolonged bleeding following wisdom teeth extraction 2 years ago. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the nose shows no abnormalities. There are several bruises on the lower extremities. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 15 g/dL
Leukocyte count 6,000/mm3
Platelet count 220,000/mm3
Bleeding time 9 minutes
Prothrombin time 13 sec
Partial thromboplastin time 55 sec
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Prolonged bleeding time" -> "Normal platelet count" -> "Normal prothrombin time" -> "Normal partial thromboplastin time" -> "Possible Von Willebrand disease" -> 70% CHAIN: "Recurrent nosebleeds" -> "Bruises on lower extremities" -> "Possible bleeding disorder" -> "Possible Von Willebrand disease" -> 80% CHAIN: "Normal hemoglobin" -> "Normal leukocyte count" -> "Normal platelet count" -> "Prolonged bleeding time" -> "Possible Von Willebrand disease" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 25-year-old man with recurrent nosebleeds, bruises on lower extremities, normal platelet count, prolonged bleeding time, and normal prothrombin time is Von Willebrand disease. This is supported by the combination of symptoms and laboratory findings, including the prolonged bleeding time and the association with spontaneous epistaxis and lower extremity bruises, which are consistent with a bleeding disorder like Von Willebrand disease.
